# BadExceptionsProcessing

<Badge type="info" text="info" /> <Badge type="info" text="off by default" />

Group: [Architecture](/rules/#architecture) · PhpStorm name: `BadExceptionsProcessingInspection`

Two smells around `try`/`catch`: a `try` block that wraps too many statements
(hard to tell which one is expected to throw), and a `catch` clause that
binds the exception to a variable but never looks at it (the error is
swallowed or its cause is lost).

## Example

```php{3,17,19}
<?php
function load(string $path) {
    try {
        $h = fopen($path, 'r');
        $line = fgets($h);
        fclose($h);
        return trim($line);
    } catch (\ErrorException $problem) {
        error_log($problem->getMessage());
    }

    try {
        $a = 1;
        // comments are not statements
        $b = 2;
        if ($a) { $b++; $b++; $b++; }
    } catch (\LogicException $ignored) {
        // nothing to do
    } catch (\DomainException | \RangeException $lost) {
        throw new \RuntimeException('cannot load');
    } catch (\TypeError $kept) {
        $log = function () use ($kept) { return $kept; };
    } catch (\Error) {
    }
}
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 3: Too many statements in this try block; extract some of them so the failing call is obvious.</li>
<li>line 17: Caught exception is silently discarded; at least log it.</li>
<li>line 19: Caught exception is dropped; log it or pass it on as the previous exception.</li>
</ul>

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "BadExceptionsProcessing": {
      "enabled": true
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file), either of:

```php
// @custos-ignore BadExceptionsProcessing

/**
 * @noinspection BadExceptionsProcessingInspection
 */
```
